THE UNITED KINGDOM: 4 RULERS SAUL → SOLOMON
Born to David and Bathsheba in Jerusalem; “the LORD loved him”. 2 Samuel 12:24–25
Chronicles records the word David received: “a son shall be born to thee, who shall be a man of rest … his name shall be Solomon”. 1 Chronicles 22:9
When David was old, his elder son Adonijah declared himself king, with Joab and Abiathar the priest on his side. 1 Kings 1:5–10

Nathan and Bathsheba reminded David of his oath that Solomon would reign. David had Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon at Gihon, riding David's own mule, and the people cried, “God save king Solomon”. 1 Kings 1:11–40

Adonijah took hold of the horns of the altar and was spared. After David's death, when he asked for Abishag, Solomon had him killed; Abiathar was sent home to Anathoth, and Joab and Shimei were put to death. “And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.” 1 Kings 1:50–53 1 Kings 2:13–46

Chronicles says only that David “made Solomon his son king over Israel”, and later that “they made Solomon the son of David king the second time”, with all David's sons submitting to him. 1 Chronicles 23:1 1 Chronicles 29:22–24
ON THE WORLD STAGE: Egypt · Tyre · Sheba · Edom · Aram (Damascus)
“Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD, and went not fully after the LORD, as did David his father”
“Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of David his father: only he sacrificed and burnt incense in high places”
Kings first praises him, with one reserve: “Solomon loved the LORD … only he sacrificed and burnt incense in high places”. 1 Kings 3:3
“when Solomon was old, … his wives turned away his heart after other gods”. He built high places for Chemosh and Molech “in the hill that is before Jerusalem”. 1 Kings 11:4–8
The LORD's word to him: “I will … rend the kingdom from thee”, yet not in his days, for David's sake, and one tribe would stay with his son. 1 Kings 11:11–13
From the textChronicles gives no verdict on Solomon, and does not tell of his foreign wives' gods or of the adversaries the LORD raised against him. 2 Chronicles 9:29–31
Nehemiah later recalled him: “among many nations was there no king like him, who was beloved of his God … nevertheless even him did outlandish women cause to sin”. Nehemiah 13:26
In the Gospels Jesus speaks of “Solomon in all his glory”, and of the queen of the south who came “to hear the wisdom of Solomon”. Matthew 6:29 Matthew 12:42

Jerusalem and the places of the reign
The united kingdom · tribe of Judah. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
Each mark sits at the year of the reign the Bible gives for it.
The house of the LORD, seven years in building, begun in his fourth year. 1 Kings 6:1 1 Kings 6:37–38
His own house, thirteen years; the house of the forest of Lebanon; the porch of pillars; the porch of judgment; a house for Pharaoh's daughter. 1 Kings 7:1–8
Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, Hazor, Megiddo, Gezer, nether Beth-horon, Baalath, Tadmor, store cities and chariot cities. 1 Kings 9:15–19
Ships at Ezion-geber, beside Eloth on the Red sea. 1 Kings 9:26
Chronicles adds that he prevailed against Hamath-zobah, built store cities in Hamath, and built Beth-horon the upper as well as the nether. 2 Chronicles 8:3–5
Na Nathan Nathan named him Jedidiah at birth, warned Bathsheba of Adonijah's bid, and anointed him with Zadok. Chronicles names “the book of Nathan the prophet” as a source for his reign.
Ah Ahijah the Shilonite “I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee”
Id Iddo the seer Named only as a source: “the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat”.
OUTSIDE THE BIBLE · ARABIC VERSION DATED AD 1314–1344 IN ITS COLOPHONS
Each ribbon joins the two accounts of one matter, passage to passage.

Age at accession not given. The temple was begun in his fourth year, “in the four hundred and eightieth year” after the Exodus (1 Kings 6:1), and finished in his eleventh (6:38). His own house took thirteen years (7:1); both were done “at the end of twenty years” (9:10).
THIELE, AS REVISED BY MCFALL AND YOUNG

Young (2003) puts Solomon's first official year in 972 or 971 BC, the start of the temple in spring 967 BC, and his death between spring and autumn 931 BC; Thiele had placed the death in 931/930 BC. McFall (2010) has Solomon succeed David in 970 BC.

Albright (1945) dated the division of the kingdom, and so Solomon's death, to 922 BC. The start, 962 BC, is our own count: Scripture's forty years (1 Kings 11:42) added to 922. Albright's own figure for Solomon's accession was not checked for this page.
Made king 1015 BC; temple founded 1012 BC, finished 1005 BC, dedicated 1004 BC; died 975 BC.
A literal count back to the Exodus
Young counts back from the start of the temple in 967 BC to an Exodus in 1446 BC, and finds the same date from the Jubilee cycles; McFall notes the figure means 479 complete years. 1 Kings 6:1 [2][3]
Wellhausen read 480 as twelve generations of forty years, one of two periods of 480 years in the Jewish chronology behind these books.[7]

Kings and Chronicles do not give Solomon's age when he began to reign.
Scripture does not name the Pharaoh whose daughter he married, nor the queen of Sheba.
The history books do not say that Solomon repented at the end of his life.
Kings says he “spake three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five” (1 Kings 4:32); the history books do not say which of them survive.
Scripture does not say how many years of his reign remained when Ahijah spoke to Jeroboam.
Jedidiah is the name Nathan gave him at birth, “because of the LORD”. 2 Samuel 12:24–25

From the textHis mother is “Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam” in 2 Samuel and “Bath-shua the daughter of Ammiel” in 1 Chronicles. The site's person record treats them as one woman, and so does this page. 2 Samuel 11:3 1 Chronicles 3:5
